title: Officials investigate fire at Mississippi police department tied to fatal shooting of Black toddler
summary:
Person arrested after fire at police department where officer who shot and killed one-year-old Kohen Wiley had worked

In the early hours of 31 October, a fire broke out at the Senatobia…

blocks.text: In the early hours of 31 October, a fire broke out at the Senatobia police department in Mississippi, which has been embroiled in controversy recently after one of its officers shot and killed Kohen Wiley, a one-year-old. Though the cause of the fire has not been reported, it is being investigated as arson by agents with the US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

In June, then Senatobia police sergeant Hunter Foster shot Kohen as he sat in his mother’s arms in a Walmart parking lot. Foster, who is white, was responding to a report of an alleged shoplifting; Kohen, his mother and the driver of the vehicle, are Black.
An arrest tied to the fire was made on Monday, but no details about the person of interest have been released. The Senatobia police department did not respond to a request for comment.
Shortly after Kohen was killed in June, activists and community members led protests, including one outside the Senatobia police department, in hopes of receiving answers about the shooting.

The Mississippi bureau of investigation, which investigated the shooting, alleged that the driver of the vehicle in which Kohen sat “drove in the direction of the officers, almost striking one”. However, civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the Wiley family, released an independent autopsy that indicated Kohen was shot from the side of the car, not the front.
In mid-October, Lynn Fitch, Mississippi’s attorney general, announced in a statement that the shooting was “justified”. Foster resigned from the police force shortly after Fitch’s statement.

“After what I’ve seen today, I’m having a difficult time understanding the word ‘justified’,” LaSandra Williams, Kohen’s paternal grandmother, said during a press conference Crump held about video footage of the shooting. “I don’t understand how it’s OK for someone to take a sweet, innocent soul – Lord knows I miss him so much.”

The shooting was just the most recent in a series of incidents involving Senatobia’s police force. The month prior to Fitch’s statement, Senatobia, which is about 40% Black, fired its police chief, who allegedly used racial slurs.

A year before Kohen was killed, at the same Walmart, an officer forced a Black woman from her car and pointed a stun gun at her in front of her children after she parked in a handicap space to wait for her grandmother, who was shopping in the store. The woman was driving a vehicle with a handicap parking tag.
And in 2023, an officer arrested and placed in a cell a 10-year-old Black boy who had urinated in public. The child was later sentenced to three months’ probation.

Kohen would have turned two last weekend. The Senatobia Committee for Accountability and Transparency, an activist group, organized a giveaway at the city’s community center to celebrate what would have been the toddler’s birthday. Families who attended received diapers, wipes, food and other items.
The ongoing investigation into the fire is being handled by the US attorney general’s office of the northern district of Mississippi.
